title: Glitchometry
method: sonification: simple squares/circles imported into an audio editor, sound effects (flanger, reverb) applied to individual colour channels
notes: Artist says flanger makes bands and reverb makes moiré. Strong fit: process-based glitch.

title: Dither Studies
method: Photoshop colour dithering of solid colours / gradients using a palette of incompatible (complementary) colours
notes: Patterns from a compression-like process (fewer colours) — close cousin of medical image quantization.

title: TIME IS NEVER WAS NEVER IS TIME
method: shot frame by frame with a 2-bit Game Boy Camera, re-filmed off a monotone Apple IIe monitor
notes: 6-minute 'silent film'; original site only on the Wayback Machine. Needs a video still.

title: NES Glitch Compilation
method: documented glitch output of a Nintendo Entertainment System (8-bit) since 2001, edited into a 30-min loop
notes: Hardware glitches (accidental, then curated). Needs a video still; original site only on the Wayback Machine.

title: flo\/\/
method: flowing video distortion; vertically scanning stream of imagery and typography
notes: Hosted on Vimeo (vimeo.com/20247975). Needs a video still.

title: System Landscapes
method: re-imagines the computer program as a landscape
notes: Same work as https://system-landscapes.rhizome.org/ and the Rhizome web archive of petracortright.com. Needs a screenshot.

title: 8 BIT WEB
method: copy-pasted code from other websites, manipulated to generate errors; 8-bit / Atari / Commodore aesthetic
notes: Glitch as 'deconstructing a website'. Needs a screenshot.

title: Data Diaries
method: QuickTime tricked into reading a computer's RAM as video data
notes: Q206 is Cory Arcangel's ARTIST page (lists Data Diaries 2003 + Bomb Iraq 2005). Method is from general knowledge, not that page — check it.

title: Bomb Iraq
method: found homemade game on a used Macintosh TV, shown as a readymade; now runs in an emulator
notes: Weak fit: not a glitch work (found game). Consider dropping or keeping as 'obsolete media' context.

title: Sky Hits the Limit
method: HDR timelapse stacked in PTGui Pro; 32-bit EXR sequence misread as 16-bit by FFmpeg
notes: 180° sky panorama, stereographic projection; doubling + glitched colours. Accidental.

title: Random World
method: corrupted Minecraft save data (binary save-file bug)
notes: Accidental.

title: pure chaos
method: jammed film advance on an Olympus 35 RD → overlapping exposures; scanned (Epson V800)
notes: Analog glitch — overlapping exposures. Accidental.

title: Pixel Noise
method: Windows XP laptop switched to 8-bit display; Euphoria screensaver error
notes: Accidental.

title: PDF ink streaks
method: Evince PDF reader glitch: USB removed while the file was open, then scrolled
notes: Ink-like streaks running down the page. Accidental.

title: Functional Fractalisator
method: drawing in pure lambda calculus; off-by-one stride-addition bugs
notes: Accidental (code bug).

title: Erosion I-VI
method: hydraulic erosion simulation on grid terrain
notes: Series of 6 (erosion-1.png … erosion-6.png). Pick one or add a row per image.

title: Blue View
method: JPG file corruption on a Canon EOS 350D photo (embedded thumbnail still correct)
notes: File corruption — closest to a data-level artifact. Accidental.

title: Chess in the Matrix
method: display glitch in KDE Plasma on a Framework laptop (cause unknown)
notes: Accidental.

title: Alteration I-VI
method: online TIFF-to-JPEG conversion of Google Street View screenshots
notes: Series of 6. Format-conversion glitch (compression) — relevant to medical image formats.

title: Roots of the problem
method: nearest-neighbour resizing bug in a custom C image library (Simple-PPM)
notes: Blue + magenta. Resizing glitch — same operation we use in data prep!

title: Ghost in the Frame
method: frame corruption: DaVinci Resolve 18 ran out of memory while editing
notes: Red, purple, yellow. Accidental.

title: Bug in the codec
method: encoding/decoding bug in a diamond-square image codec
notes: Codec glitch. Accidental.

title: Orange Shift
method: JMP packed-circles chart of Mastodon instances with orange labels accidentally left on
notes: Data-visualization 'glitch'. Accidental.

title: Behind Bars
method: DVB-T TV stick with EyeTV; detuned + wiggled antenna
notes: Warm colours, soft image with sharp artifacts. Signal interference — like acquisition artifacts in scans.

title: Void of the Future
method: iOS Photos loading glitch swapped year-view thumbnails for blank squares
notes: Light grey + black. Accidental.

title: fontgedoens
method: Haskell + OpenGL bitmap-font rendering; vertices got scrambled
notes: Image file is named salat.png. Accidental.

title: Crumbling Giant
method: After Effects / Apple Motion scene after deleting a transparent pixel asset → black squares
notes: Accidental.

title: Glyphs
method: row/column swap when rendering a font test
notes: Accidental.

title: Viewscape
method: Rust/OpenGL shader debugging; view vector shown as colour after a missing camera uniform
notes: Described as dreamy / trippy. Accidental.

title: Memories Unravelling I-IX
method: screenshots of a corrupted GNOME default desktop background
notes: Series of 9; blocky patterns. Accidental.

title: Moment before the infinite loop
method: live-coded vertex shader in KodeLife; accidental infinite loop crashed the IDE
notes: Accidental.

title: Collapsing Waves
method: Wave Function Collapse with adjacent-pixel constraints (rendered in HTML tables)
notes: Animated GIF — use one frame.

title: melting a e s t h e t i c
method: pixel-art landscape generator (coastlines, reflections); bug during palette experiments
notes: Title references vaporwave-style 'aesthetic' — a bridge to the Internet Aesthetics project.

title: Not Quite Interpolation
method: ray tracer texture mapping with broken interpolation (university homework)
notes: Accidental.

title: Subdivision
method: Barnes-Hut tree for a galaxy simulation with the wrong child-cell offset (width/2 instead of width/4)
notes: Accidental.

title: Psychedelic Rainbow
method: decoding glitch from a file-parsing bug in gpu_jpeg2k (JPEG 2000 codec)
notes: JPEG 2000 is also used in medical imaging (DICOM) — interesting link.

title: Traversing Berlin
method: Berlin transit (VBB GTFS) stop coordinates plotted as SVG paths using truncated lat/long digits
notes: Data-visualization glitch.

title: Disco Time
method: force-directed graph drawing where old edges were never cleared
notes: Accidental.

title: The Stanford Iceberg
method: OpenGL vertex buffer objects with incorrect indices (Stanford 3D model)
notes: Accidental.

title: ppt.xxx
method: Ruby scripts scrape PowerPoint slideshows, export slides as images, glitch them, re-upload
notes: Intentional, automated glitching ('add noise to signal'). Needs a screenshot of a glitched slide.

title: 00FFFF - Pixelation Routine
method: data manipulation and pixelation / corruption routines; Google Earth hacked with a malfunctioning video card
notes: Flash — may not run anymore; look for archived screenshots.

title: Monogrid 0.1
method: two algorithms on one surface: one pushes pixels out of place, the other returns them
notes: Asendorf is known for pixel sorting. Live at monogrid.rhizome.org — screenshot a frame.

title: troika
method: every object in the Rhizome database shown as one pixel; colour set by keywords and user activity
notes: Weak fit for 'distortion' — it's a data-as-pixels visualization. Good for the 'image as data' angle.

title: Nowash
method: interactive pixel composition ('wash the image')
notes: Description is poetic, not technical. Check if it's still viewable.

title: Selbst-los / Self-less
method: an image of the artist dissolves pixel by pixel as users visit
notes: Flash (deprecated). Rhizome keeps static files. Portrait disappearing — interesting next to body scans.

title: Pscan Derivatives
method: 'Pixelscapes' viewed through an interactive magnifying lens applet
notes: Minimal pixel art, not really a glitch. Java applet probably won't run.

title: liquid_eden
method: visitors' clicks shift the pixels of a lily image downward toward dissolution
notes: Java (likely broken). Collective, intentional distortion.

title: IPicons
method: icon generated from an IP address: first 3 numbers = R, G, B; 4th = pattern
notes: Weak fit for glitch — but a neat 'data → colour' example (same 0-255 RGB range as our pixels).

title: Recombinant Icon
method: self-modifying GUI icon based on Turing's idea of a machine reading and changing its own state
notes: Shockwave (deprecated). Rhizome keeps static files.

title: Illicit images
method: pixel data of web images encrypted with strong cryptography → images look like random static
notes: Strong fit: data turned into pure noise. Rhizome keeps static files.

title: ap0202
method: self-modifying code across networked nodes that only displays its own changing code
notes: Code display, not image distortion. Probably drop unless you want a 'code as material' example.
